heroHeadline: Explosion Injures 13 in Taiwan (Aug 23); China Conducts First-Ever Public SLBM Test (Jul 6, South Pacific); Carrier Fujian Transits Strait (Jun 22); Taiwan Fires HIMARS Westward for First Time (Jun 10); PLA Sorties Moderate to 2-22/Day Range; TSMC Posts Record Q2 Profit
heroSubtitle: Since our last update (June 7), PLA daily ADIZ activity around Taiwan moderated to a 2-22 sortie/day range — no new record has been set since June 4's all-time non-exercise high of 32 sorties. But the six-week window produced several higher-significance developments. On June 10, Taiwan fired US-supplied HIMARS rockets westward into the Taiwan Strait for the first time, demonstrating deep-strike reach toward the Fujian coast. On June 17, G7 leaders meeting in Évian reaffirmed opposition to coercion across the Taiwan Strait. China's newest carrier, the electromagnetic-catapult-equipped Fujian, transited the Strait on June 22 — its first passage since December 2025. On July 1, Taiwan detained two Super Micro executives in a widening probe into alleged smuggling of Nvidia AI chips to China. Most significantly, on July 6, China conducted its first publicly disclosed submarine-launched ballistic missile test, firing a reported JL-3-class missile into the South Pacific near the Kiribati/Tuvalu EEZ — drawing protests from New Zealand and Australia, while Beijing called it 'routine' training. The most recent MND report (July 16) shows 5 PLA sorties, 7 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships, with 3 sorties crossing into central and southwestern ADIZ sectors. On the economic front, Taiwan's outlook strengthened further: Academia Sinica raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 10.16% (July 13) — the first double-digit prediction from a major forecaster — and TSMC reported record Q2 2026 net income of NT$706.56 billion (+77.4% YoY) with an additional $100 billion Arizona investment commitment (July 16). The $14 billion US arms package remains 'under review' with no new public resolution since Secretary Rubio's June 3 testimony.
